subject: Agriculture
title: Organic Matter
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Organic Matter.

hook.text: Organic matter makes up only 5% of most soils—but it drives almost everything that matters.

buildup.text: Dead leaves, roots, insect bodies, and manure all decompose into a dark substance called humus.

discovery.text: Humus holds water like a sponge—up to six times its weight—and slowly releases nutrients to plant roots.

twist.text: Tilling soil exposes organic matter to air, speeding decomposition. Intensive farming burns through humus fast.

climax.text: Rebuilding organic matter takes years of cover cropping and compost. Losing it takes one bad season.

punchline.text: Five percent of the soil does fifty percent of the work.

quiz.question: What is humus?
options: Decomposed organic matter that holds water and nutrients in soil

details.summary: Soil organic matter is the decomposed remains of plants, animals, and microorganisms that typically make up 1-6% of topsoil by weight. Despite this small fraction, organic matter drives soil fertility, water retention, structure, and biological activity.
details.whyItMatters: Organic matter is the single most important indicator of soil health. Each 1% increase in organic matter allows soil to hold an additional 20,000 gallons of water per acre and dramatically improves nutrient availability for crops.
takeaways: Organic matter is only 1-6% of topsoil by weight but drives most soil functions
Each 1% increase in organic matter holds 20,000 additional gallons of water per acre
Humus—the stable end product of decomposition—persists in soil for centuries

faq.question: Why is soil organic matter so important despite being such a small fraction?
faq.answer: Organic matter acts as a sponge for water, a reservoir for nutrients, a food source for soil organisms, and a glue that holds soil particles into stable aggregates. It increases cation exchange capacity, buffers pH, and releases nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur as it decomposes.

faq.question: How can farmers increase soil organic matter?
faq.answer: Adding compost, growing cover crops, reducing tillage, leaving crop residues on fields, and integrating livestock all build organic matter. It takes years of consistent practice to raise organic matter by even 1%, but the benefits to water retention, fertility, and yield are substantial.
